items.problem: Hardcoded literal Foreground="White" (and white icon Fill/glyphs) carried from the UWP camera overlay renders invisible white-on-white in WinUI 3, because the migrated app defaults to the system Light theme and ApplicationPageBackgroundThemeBrush is white while the preview surface is blank/absent.
items.evidence: Generated MainPage.xaml (session-log.txt ~1303-1342, 2538): StatusText Foreground="White" and button Setter Foreground=White over Grid Background={ThemeResource ApplicationPageBackgroundThemeBrush}; scorer discrepancies.json ids 'blank-fallback-text'/'invisible-disabled-buttons'; migration-score.json verdict partial (50).
items.root_cause: Skill teaches resource-reference migration (StaticResource->ThemeResource) but never warns about hardcoded literal colours or the UWP(dark)->WinUI(Light) default-theme shift.
items.change: Added a 'Hardcoded literal colours assume the wrong default theme' subsection under the ThemeResource pattern: explains UWP media/camera overlays hardcode white-on-dark, WinUI 3 defaults to Light, so white content goes invisible; fix is theme brushes ({ThemeResource TextFillColorPrimaryBrush}) or keep the contrasting dark container.
items.expected_effect: Agent replaces literal white foreground/glyphs with theme-aware brushes (or preserves the dark container), so migrated camera/media pages render visible content on the Light default theme.
items.falsifiable_check: On re-run, generated XAML contains no Foreground="White" directly on the page background; the camera-less screenshot shows visible content (buttons/fallback) instead of a blank white frame; requirement #0 goes partial->pass.

items.problem: The defensive-UI fallback the agent added was Visible but invisible in practice (white-on-white), so the page still captured blank. The rule secured that a fallback exists, not that it is seen.
items.evidence: SKILL.md defensive-UI Rule (lines 221-224) was followed (StatusText set Visible) yet discrepancies.json 'blank-fallback-text': 'renders white-on-white and is invisible'.
items.root_cause: 'Visible fallback' was under-specified: it didn't require contrast against WinUI 3's default Light page background.
items.change: Sharpened the existing Rule with a clause: '"Visible" means contrast-visible, not just Visibility=Visible' — use a theme-aware foreground ({ThemeResource TextFillColorPrimaryBrush} or default), never a hardcoded Foreground="White" copied from a media-overlay source; cross-links the new PATTERNS subsection.
items.expected_effect: Defensive fallbacks (the device-absent path common to headless validation) render a readable message instead of an invisible one.
items.falsifiable_check: On re-run, the device-absent fallback TextBlock uses a theme/default foreground and is legible in the captured screenshot (non-blank frame).

deferred_to_human: Tier-1 idea (not auto-applied, false-positive risk): Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 could WARN on literal Foreground="White"/white Fill in migrated XAML, but white-over-dark-container usage is legitimate so a context-free grep would be noisy; left as prose.
